meta.status: drafted — needs reconciliation against the recipe tag schema; wheat/soy decision open
meta.single_source_of_truth: This list is THE one controlled vocabulary. The personal-fast UI, the recipe tagger, and the recommender's hard filter all import it. It is never edited in one surface and not the others.
meta.ambiguity_rule: When a recipe is genuinely ambiguous, the tagger errs toward INCLUDING the category (recipe filtered out). Wrongly hiding a fine dish is a mild cost; wrongly recommending a forbidden one is the real failure.

open_decisions.note: The shipped recipe database extends fast_codes with `wheat` and `soy` (110 rows) beyond the seven categories. Decide: first-class fast categories (nine) or allergen tags reused as filters. Must be one documented source of truth shared with the allergen list.

EF complete abstinence permits meat broth (B1); the `meat` tag includes broth (safe-erring). The obligation-layer filter and the personal-fast filter may need different meat scopes — resolve BEFORE the single-filter consolidation is built.
Where exactly trace flavoring ends (e.g. wine simmered into a long-cooked sauce — proposed: trips `alcohol` if named as an ingredient). Reviewer to set.

categories.label: Fish & seafood
categories.means: Aquatic animals: finfish, shellfish, crustaceans, mollusks

categories.label: Dairy
categories.means: Milk and milk products: milk, cheese, butter, cream, yogurt

categories.label: Alcohol
categories.means: Alcoholic beverages, and alcohol added as a cooking ingredient
includes_derivatives: wine/beer/spirits cooked into a dish as a named ingredient
excludes: trace flavoring (e.g. vanilla extract) — see trace rule

categories.label: Oil
categories.means: Added culinary oils and fats of plant origin (olive, seed, vegetable)
excludes: fat naturally in whole foods (nuts, olives, avocado)
animal fats route to their source: lard → meat, butter → dairy

categories.label: Sweets
categories.means: Dish class: desserts, confections, sweetened treats
excludes: incidental sugar in a savory dish — dish-class rule
categories.note: Dish-driven, not ingredient-driven: a teaspoon of sugar in a savory sauce does NOT trip it. The tagging pipeline must support both modes — easiest place for the tagger to be built wrong.

trace_rule: Derivatives that are a structural part of the dish count (a soup built on chicken stock is `meat`; a sauce with a named pour of wine is `alcohol`). Flavoring agents present only in trace amounts do not trip the category — standing example: vanilla extract does not flag `alcohol`.

rules: A custom free-text commitment is tracked and displayed for the user's own observance.
It does NOT filter recipes — unless the user maps it onto an existing category, in which case it filters normally.
The UI says plainly which custom commitments meal suggestions can and can't account for. Silent non-enforcement is the dishonest failure mode.

obligation_layer_reuse: A day ruled as abstinence is mechanically a system-applied avoid:meat with fish allowed — the reason meat and fish are separate categories. Holds only if meat/fish definitions stay canonically consistent; see meat-broth-scopes open decision.
orthodox_bridge: The list maps onto Orthodox fasting tiers (meat / dairy+eggs / fish / wine / oil) — why oil and alcohol are in a Roman v1. Refinements when Orthodox lands: wine vs broader alcohol; oil as added olive oil specifically.
